title.zh: 掩码有限网格环向体积

summary: Compute the toroidally revolved volume represented by an explicit finite R/Z grid and a caller-supplied core mask.

capability: Reduce an explicit masked R/Z mesh to its toroidally revolved volume.
operation: finite-grid toroidal volume reduction with an explicit mask
R coordinates, cell widths and core mask -> scalar volume
discovery.model: Discrete cell sum of 2*pi*R*dR*dZ*core_mask; no equilibrium solve or boundary reconstruction.
discovery.geometry: Axisymmetric R/Z mesh with axis 0 radial and axis 1 vertical; the mask and coordinates are supplied explicitly.
discovery.boundary: The mask values select or weight included grid locations; no implicit boundary, extrapolation or topology inference is performed.

identity.relation: finite R/Z coordinates and an explicit core mask to the toroidally revolved grid volume
identity.definition: Form 2*pi*R*dR*dZ elementwise, multiply by core_mask using NumPy broadcasting, sum all elements and project the scalar to a Python float.
identity.geometry: Axisymmetric R/Z mesh; axis 0 is radial and axis 1 is vertical; R and spacings use metres and the output uses cubic metres.
identity.coordinates: R contains major-radius coordinates at the supplied grid locations; no coordinate transformation or mesh reconstruction is performed.
identity.boundary: The caller-supplied mask defines the included region. Numeric mask values are weights, and values outside a Boolean interpretation are not clipped.
assumptions: R is a real array whose entries and dR/dZ use one consistent length unit, normally metres.
dR and dZ are uniform cell widths represented by scalar values.
core_mask is Boolean or numeric and is broadcast-compatible with R.
The caller has already solved or selected any equilibrium and boundary state represented by core_mask.
The finite cell sum is a measure for the supplied mesh; it is not a convergence or physical-shape guarantee.

inputs.name: R
inputs.description: Major-radius coordinate array for the finite R/Z grid.
inputs.constraints: Used as supplied by NumPy arithmetic; the implementation does not sort, validate finiteness or infer a mesh.

inputs.name: dR
inputs.constraints: Used as supplied; zero, negative and non-finite values are not separately rejected.

inputs.name: dZ
inputs.constraints: Used as supplied; zero, negative and non-finite values are not separately rejected.

inputs.name: core_mask
inputs.description: Caller-supplied core or limiter mask, optionally carrying numeric cell weights.
inputs.constraints: Broadcasting follows NumPy. No implicit mask is constructed and values are not clipped to [0,1].

outputs.name: volume
outputs.constraints: Finite, NaN or infinite according to the supplied arithmetic; no physical validity filter is applied.

preconditions: The caller supplies a finite-grid R/Z measure and a mask representing the region to include.
R, dR and dZ use one consistent length unit, and the caller accepts the discrete cell-sum approximation.
supported: Numeric masks providing explicit per-cell weights.
NumPy-broadcastable mask shapes and the declared finite/non-finite arithmetic branches.
excluded: Equilibrium solving, limiter or separatrix construction, and topology inference.
Nonuniform-cell quadrature, mesh convergence estimation and geometric boundary correction.
A claim that the returned sum is a physically validated plasma volume for an arbitrary caller mask.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Python and NumPy arithmetic or broadcasting exceptions propagate for unsupported operands or incompatible shapes; the callable performs no separate domain validation.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Unexpected NumPy arithmetic errors propagate and no fallback mask or mesh is selected.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is one direct reduction with no iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial volume is returned after an arithmetic or broadcasting failure.

example.description: Sum two selected cells on a 2x2 R/Z grid with uniform widths.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import plasma_volume
R = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, 2.0]])
mask = np.array([[True, False], [True, False]])
volume = plasma_volume(R, dR=0.5, dZ=0.25, core_mask=mask)
np.testing.assert_allclose(volume, 2.0 * np.pi * (1.0 + 2.0) * 0.5 * 0.25)
example.expected: The selected cells produce the scalar volume 2*pi*(1+2)*0.5*0.25 cubic metres.

scope: Exact arithmetic for Boolean and numeric masks on the declared finite-grid relation.
NumPy broadcasting failure, zero spacing, non-finite arithmetic and float32 coordinate rows.
Input immutability and Python-float scalar projection.
The complete twelve-row candidate source-fidelity denominator is retained in the incoming packet; state-only missing-profile rows are outside this explicit public port contract.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The incoming candidate's exact comparison establishes source behavior parity for its twelve declared rows, while the maintained direct tests establish this explicit source-free R/dR/dZ/core_mask relation. Neither establishes independent physical correctness, mesh convergence, boundary reconstruction or human scientific acceptance.
known_limitations: The cell sum inherits the caller's grid and mask; it does not construct or validate an equilibrium boundary.
Zero, negative, NaN and infinite inputs follow NumPy arithmetic and may produce non-finite output.
Numeric mask weights are intentional and are not interpreted as a Boolean core classification.
